nodes.label: escapeHtml() Before DOM Insertion Convention
nodes.rationale: LLM/extraction-derived text is untrusted output; escaping before DOM insertion prevents it from being interpreted as markup/script.

nodes.label: Groq API Key Never Persisted Invariant
nodes.norm_label: groq api key never persisted invariant
nodes.rationale: Keeps the Groq key out of any durable artifact (disk, logs, audit trail) so a compromised log/audit file can never leak credentials; key lives only in the Flask session and outbound Authorization header.

nodes.label: Cross-Check Disagreement Forces Exception Invariant
nodes.rationale: A sampled dual-extraction disagreement is the strongest available accuracy signal, so it must override any other passing check rather than being averaged away.

nodes.label: Explicit Abstractor Resolution Invariant
nodes.rationale: Exceptions exist because automation was insufficiently confident; auto-resolving them would defeat the purpose of the human-in-the-loop fail-safe.

nodes.label: NormalizedField Provenance Invariant
nodes.rationale: Recording coding_reference_version and spec_version keeps registry submissions reproducible under audit even as coding standards and specs evolve.

nodes.label: RAG-Grounded Normalization Invariant
nodes.rationale: Constrains the LLM to retrieved candidates only so coding-standard mapping is grounded rather than a guess; below-threshold candidates route to exception instead of a fabricated code.

nodes.label: Source-Span Verification Invariant
nodes.rationale: Prevents any field from being trusted solely on LLM output; extraction_engine.py independently re-checks the quoted excerpt occurs verbatim in the raw document before acceptance.

nodes.label: Synthetic-Only Sample Data Invariant
nodes.rationale: Sample/reference data must stay synthetic so the POC never handles real PHI outside a governed production deployment.

nodes.label: Coding Standard Drift Risk
nodes.rationale: Coding standards (e.g. ICD-10) change over time; versioned mappings keep historical records correctly interpretable.

nodes.label: PHI Handling Non-Functional Requirement
nodes.rationale: Source documents are PHI; access scoping plus an independent repository guard blocking PHI-shaped writes protect the POC's synthetic-data boundary.

nodes.label: Sampled Dual-Extraction Cross-Check Trade-off
nodes.rationale: 100% dual-extraction would be too costly; a tunable sampling rate per field criticality trades some coverage for cost while still bounding risk.

nodes.label: apply_validation_gate() Override Priority
nodes.rationale: Checking cross-check disagreement first, even though it's conceptually the last of three checks, guarantees it can never be masked by an otherwise-passing confidence or rule check.

nodes.label: Token-Usage Estimation Caveat
nodes.rationale: Threading real Groq usage.total_tokens through every call site (classification, per-field extraction, per-field normalization, cross-check) would be invasive; a response-length/4 estimate is used instead and explicitly tagged as an estimate.

nodes.label: Synchronous-per-Document Pipeline (Async Deferred)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous per-document processing is adequate at POC scale; the async 202/status contract is deferred until real batch volume justifies it.

nodes.label: Context Trimming Policy
nodes.rationale: Keeps sub-agents focused on the current change rather than re-deriving already-resolved context as transcripts grow.
